name: asconfig-schema

optimizeLevel.description: How much to focus on optimizing code.

shrinkLevel.description: How much to focus on shrinking code size.

converge.description: Re-optimizes until no further improvements can be made.

baseDir.description: Specifies the base directory of input and output files.

textFile.description: Specifies the WebAssembly text output file (.wat).

sourceMap.description: Enables source map generation. Optionally takes the URL.

runtime.description: Specifies the runtime variant to include in the program.

noUnsafe.description: Disallows the use of unsafe features in user code.

debug.description: Enables debug information in emitted binaries.

noAssert.description: Replaces assertions with just their value without trapping.

noEmit.description: Performs compilation as usual but does not emit code.

noExportMemory.description: Does not export the memory as 'memory'.

initialMemory.description: Sets the initial memory size in pages.

maximumMemory.description: Sets the maximum memory size in pages.

sharedMemory.description: Declare memory as shared. Requires maximumMemory.

zeroFilledMemory.description: Assume that imported memory is zero filled. Requires importMemory.

memoryBase.description: Sets the start offset of compiler-generated static memory.

importTable.description: Imports the function table provided as 'env.table'.

exportStart.description: Exports the start function instead of calling it implicitly.

lib.description: Adds one or multiple paths to custom library components.

path.description: Adds one or multiple paths to package resolution.

use.description: Aliases a global object under another name.

trapMode.description: Sets the trap mode to use.

runPasses.description: Specifies additional Binaryen passes to run.

noValidate.description: Skips validating the module using Binaryen.

enable.description: Enables WebAssembly features that are disabled by default.

disable.description: Disables WebAssembly features that are enabled by default.

transform.description: Specifies the path to a custom transform to 'require'.

pedantic.description: Make yourself sad for no good reason.

stats.description: Prints measuring information on I/O and compile times.

tableBase.description: Sets the start offset of emitted table elements.

wasm.description: Uses the specified Wasm binary of the compiler.

description:
The project configuration builds on **base‑asconfig.json** and compiles the two TypeScript entry points `src/main.ts` and `src/util.ts`.  Optimisation is fully enabled (‑‑optimize, level 3) with aggressive shrinking (level 2) and convergence, using `src` as the base directory.  The compiled WebAssembly binary will be written to `build/app.wasm` together with its text format at `build/app.wat`, and a source‑map file will be generated at `build/app.map`.  Bindings are produced for both ES‑modules and raw output.  The runtime variant is the minimal build; unsafe features are allowed, debugging information is disabled, assertions are stripped, and code emission proceeds normally.  Memory is imported from the environment, not exported, initialised to 256 pages, with a maximum of 1024 pages and shared memory also set to 1024 pages; the imported memory is assumed zero‑filled and the static memory base is zero.  The function table is imported and exported, with the start function exported under the name `start`.  Library paths include `node_modules/@as/library`; module resolution will search `node_modules` and `libs`; the global object is aliased as `globalThis`.  Trap handling is set to *allow*.  Additional Binaryen passes `--disable-opt` and `--strip-debug` are run, validation is performed, and the WebAssembly features *simd* and *threads* are enabled while *gc* is disabled.  A custom transform is loaded from `transforms/customTransform.js`.  Pedantic mode is off, statistics are printed, terminal colours are enabled, and runtime helpers are exported.  The stack size is configured to 524 288 bytes, a low‑memory limit of 65 536 bytes is enforced, the table base is zero, and the compiler will use the binary at `bin/compiler.wasm`.

Two build targets are defined.  The **release** target mirrors the main optimisation settings (‑‑optimize, level 3, shrink 2) and writes its output to `dist/release/app.wasm`; it disables source‑maps and debugging.  The **debug** target turns optimisation off (level 0, shrink 0), outputs to `dist/debug/app.wasm`, enables source‑maps and debugging, and uses the *incremental* runtime variant.
